correctness.rationale: The proof enumerates all allowed occupancy patterns, producing PF4(G) as the union of the simply connected two-skeleton of the join of part-discrete complexes and contractible stars F_i. Each intersection F_i with the preceding union is the connected bipartite graph K_{n_i,N-n_i}, because all pairwise star overlaps already lie inside the skeleton. Integral Mayer–Vietoris gives split H2 extensions by free H1 of these intersections and no other reduced homology. The rank simplifies exactly to e2+e3−(r−1)(N−1). Van Kampen supplies simple connectivity, and Hurewicz/Whitehead upgrades integral homology to a wedge of two-spheres. An independent finite checker directly verifies forbidden P4s, occupancy faces, and F2 homology for 336 tuples (r=3..5,N<=9). Bounded computation is corroboration only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The published bipartite formula cannot dominate arbitrary three-or-more-part graphs. The three-path case cannot imply the four-path case. originality.rationale: The July 2026 primary manuscript states the general sphere-wedge property as Conjecture 4.7 and settles the complete-bipartite cases for arbitrary path length and multipartite P3, but not general multipartite P4. Its face-decomposition lemma is duly credited. A separate 2021 classification concerns higher-independence (bounded induced component size) complexes, which are not the same as four-path-free complexes. published-finding corpus targeted searches, primary-text comparisons, and recoverable local historical claims disclosed no statement that implies this infinite-family integral homotopy formula. Residual risk of unindexed manuscripts is acknowledged.
residual_risks: The published-finding corpus embedding search is non-exhaustive and some unpublished or unindexed prior source may cover the theorem.
The public 2026 manuscript might have independently developed unpublished extensions after its first posting; these cannot be excluded from publicly checked text.

value.rationale: This resolves the full P4 parameter layer, for every complete multipartite graph with at least three nonempty parts, of a natural explicitly stated July 2026 homotopy conjecture. It gives a closed integral homotopy multiplicity, handles all nonuniform sizes and nonpure/nonsequential Cohen-Macaulay examples such as K_{3,3,1}, and is not an isolated example, routine parity observation or previously published table value.
